recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. Revisit only if FHIR-I later decides to prescribe exact null placement, Period boundary handling, or Range ordering for specific search parameters.
issue_request: FHIR-12205 was a Published/Not Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I clarification asking how sorting should work for complex values such as Range/Period and for missing/null values, with Observation.effective[x] date sorting as the motivating example. The resolution was to generalize the existing reasonable-order guidance across datatypes and leave sort order implementation-dependent rather than prescribing exact rules.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git-svn commit a76403735f4636f667e40a703e5cc865f0fd8f94, '#12205 - note about sort order', corresponding to Jira's svn revision 10272 comment. That commit edited source/search.html to split the sorting consistency paragraph out of the string-only bullet so it applied generally.
additional_context: The original Zulip thread 'Observation date sorting' matches the Jira question and shows the Period-boundary and missing-effective ambiguity that prompted tracker 12205. Later Published issues refined the same search section without reversing FHIR-12205: FHIR-19692 added explicit discretion for repeated and complex elements, and FHIR-39398 added date/Period server-defined wording. Both related issues already have combined-branch audit commits.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/search.html already says servers have discretion for repeated and complex elements, that exact cross-server sorting consistency rules are not specified, and that date sorting over non-singleton source data such as Period is server-defined. Adding a separate null-ordering rule would exceed the approved FHIR-12205 resolution.
